key_insight: A meta-learning framework lets O‑RAN controllers quickly adapt handover policies (choose between Conditional and Traditional HOs and tune parameters) across cells, substantially reducing failures and delay while controlling signaling and resource use.
problem_solved: Addresses high handover failure rates, latency and the signaling/resource trade-offs of Traditional (THO) and Conditional Handovers (CHO) in dense, high‑frequency NextG deployments by enabling fast transfer and per‑cell adaptation of HO decisions.
method: Meta‑learning across cells to learn transferable initial policies/priors that speed up local adaptation to varying mobility and radio conditions.
Online adaptation in the O‑RAN near‑RT RIC: a decision agent selects HO type and parameters, balancing reliability vs signaling/resource costs via a reward function.
Large‑scale evaluation (countrywide mobility traces / realistic O‑RAN testbed simulation) demonstrating robustness and reduced failures/latency while controlling signaling overhead.
impact: Shows how meta‑learning can solve non‑stationary, distributed control problems in wireless networks and provides a practical blueprint for deploying ML agents in O‑RAN for real‑time radio management.
visual_elements: Timeline/sequence diagram contrasting THO (reactive) vs CHO (proactive reservation + user execution).
Flowchart of the meta‑learning loop: meta‑training across cells → fast local adaptation → RIC decision/action → feedback.
Bar/line charts comparing failure rate, handover latency, and signaling overhead before vs after the proposed method.
Map/heatmap of cell‑level improvements (e.g., drop in failures or latency) across a countrywide deployment.
paper_title: Meta-Learning-Based Handover Management in NextG O-RAN
paper_authors: Michail Kalntis, George Iosifidis, José Suárez-Varela, Andra Lutu, Fernando A. Kuipers
